question_text: An investigator is studying the structural characteristics of pathogenic viruses. Cell cultures infected by different viruses are observed under a scanning electron microscope. The most likely virus that has infected this cell sample can cause which of the following conditions?

                    ### Question
                    An investigator is studying the structural characteristics of pathogenic viruses. Cell cultures infected by different viruses are observed under a scanning electron microscope. One of the cell samples is infected by a virus that has an envelope composed of nuclear membrane molecules. The most likely virus that has infected this cell sample can cause which of the following conditions?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Yellow fever
opb. Shingles
opc. Erythema infectiosum
opd. Ebola
ope. Condylomata acuminata

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The virus that uses nuclear membrane molecules for its envelope and is most likely to have infected the cell sample is the Varicella-zoster virus, a member of the Herpesviridae family, which causes shingles. This is supported by evidence linking Human herpesvirus 3 to Herpes zoster disease. Other viruses listed (Yellow fever virus, Parvovirus B19, Ebola virus, and Human Papillomavirus) do not use nuclear membrane molecules for their envelopes and are not members of the Herpesviridae family.
